bounded_contexts.name: cloud-intelligence
bounded_contexts.description: OAuth subscription-pool gateway (ADR-0384 Path B): multiplexes the AI-agent fleet over OAuth-subscription-backed pooled provider credentials. The kernel crate owns the pure seat-pool state machine (round-robin / fill-first selection, RAII SeatLease concurrency guard, per-seat failure-count blacklist threshold, Released / RefreshFailed / RateLimited429 outcomes, owned policy-engine AuthzGate seam). The rest crate owns the axum reverse proxy, async reqwest::Client (shared, TLS-amortised), upstream OAuth singleflight per handle (broadcast-channel coalescer), SSE streaming passthrough with pool-lease lifecycle extended to span the full streamed response (SseStreamWithLease), hop-by-hop header enforcement, 1 MiB body-size limit, EventSink fan-out trait. The authz-cedar-adapter crate is a transient adapter that wires the bundled cloud-intelligence.cedar fixture to the kernel AuthzGate seam until the owned policy-engine service is the default binding. The app crate is the composition root: wires kernel + policy-engine adapter + in-process stubs + shared reqwest::Client into build_app() -> Arc<AppState>, and serves the axum router via the cloud-intelligence binary.

ips.title: Cloud Intelligence production design-spec package and clean-room key-pool reverse-proxy implementation (kernel state machine + axum SSE-passthrough rest adapter + app composition layer, owned secret-provider-sourced keys, two-realm constant-time auth, OTel-aligned metrics, hash-only logging, OpenAPI 3.2.0 / AsyncAPI 3.1.0 / proto3 contracts, policy-engine adapter fixture, OpenSLO, runbooks, threat-model + design dossier)

adrs.title: Per-microservice flat layout; new microservices ship under microservices/<ms>/

cloud-intelligence gateway production design: provider-abstraction + canonical OpenAI-compatible surface, key-pool resilience state machine + per-tenant pools honoring Retry-After, Bedrock-shaped immutable audit + default-off body logging, OpenSLO SLI set

hyperscaler_inv_coverage.circuit_breaker: Per-key failure-count blacklist threshold + jittered cooldown in oya-cloud-intelligence-kernel acts as a per-upstream-key circuit breaker (open on N consecutive failures, half-open on cooldown expiry via lazy restore). Per-provider fallback chain is implemented via the group routing layer: multiple groups can serve the same channel class with independent pools, and the failover loop rotates across keys within a group. No cross-process shared breaker state is claimed.
hyperscaler_inv_coverage.tenant_rate_limit: The gateway authenticates ingress proxy-keys and implements per-key failure isolation. Per-tenant token-bucket rate limiting is tracked as a deferred item at registry/placeholder-debt/adr-follow-ups.yaml#adr-0373-cloud-intelligence-per-tenant-rate-limit and surfaced as Unimplemented::PerTenantRateLimit (501) when invoked.
hyperscaler_inv_coverage.golden_signals: OTel-aligned metrics via structured tracing events expose request outcomes, per-key success/failure, retries, upstream latency, and active-key gauge (oya_cloud_intelligence_*) with Prometheus text exposition at /metrics. Scrape wiring to Alloy/VictoriaMetrics is deployment-time.
hyperscaler_inv_coverage.error_budget_burn: OpenSLO error-rate and availability SLO files authored at microservices/cloud-intelligence/slos/. Burn-rate alert wiring to VictoriaMetrics is deployment-time; no live SLO burn is claimed for the local-foundation phase.

pod_runtime_tier_justification: The agent-dispatch gateway brokers pooled provider credentials and is intended Tier-2 isolation (first-party application microservice, runc). No runtime pod deployment is claimed for the local-foundation phase; tier is retained as the intended isolation class.

capacity_model.notes: The gateway is a stateless reverse proxy (pooled keys are ephemeral in-memory cache resolved through owned secret-provider handles). Storage is 0 GB (no gateway-owned persistent state). Outbound HTTP connections are the upstream provider connections per active tenant. CPU/RAM are conservative design estimates for the local-foundation phase; measured baselines replace these once the gateway is live.
